description.narrative:
The Literacy Champions Fellowship is a transformative two-year program dedicated to improving early literacy while empowering youthas agents of change in their communities. This initiative operates across diverse communities and libraries, directly addressing literacy challenges in underserved areas and fostering a culture of learning and leadership.
Core Training: Fellows undergo hands-on training in early literacy techniques, teaching through play, teaching at the right level and personal development, equipping them to inspire and nurture young learners effectively.
Community Engagement: Fellows lead community book clinics, working with 15–25 children per session in interactive literacy activities that ignite a love for reading, build self-expression, and boost confidence.
Literacy on Wheels: This mobile initiative brings literacy sessions and reading materials to children in remote, hard-to-reach areas,ensuring no child is left behind. Fellows ride bicycles to deliver resources and sessionsto communities without libraries or accessto educational tools.
Advocacy and Holistic Development: Fellows create enabling environments for literacy by engaging parents, local leaders, and educators. This approach ensures holistic child development while advocating for inclusive, community-supported education.
Boot Camp and Graduation: Fellows participate in an intensive week-long boot camp, where they network with organizations, refine their skills, and explore innovative literacy approaches. Theprogram concludes with a celebratory graduation ceremony on International Literacy Day, recognizing fellows' achievements and launching them as literacy advocates in their communities.
Alumni Network: Graduates join an active alumni group, ensuring continued engagement, mentorship, and advocacy for literacy.

participating-org.narrative:
Founded in 2021 by Mago Hasfa, Read to Learn Foundation is an indigenous Ugandan women-led nonprofit organization dedicated to early literacy development. Our approach centers on creating sustainable, community-driven interventions to empower underservedcommunities and foster a culture of lifelong learning.
Vision: We envision a world where every child has equitable access to the right startin their educational journey, laying a strong foundation for lifelong learning, opportunities, and success.
Mission: To empower diverse communities with the tools, skills, and resources needed to deliver effective early literacy programs, ensuring every child, regardless of background or circumstance, has the opportunity to thrive academically and socially.
Core Values: - Inclusion: We champion diversity, equity, and respect by engaging with communities across socio-economic, cultural, and ability spectrums. Our commitment is to provide quality education for every child, including those facing unique challenges. - Openness: We embrace transparency and honest communication, fostering trust and meaningful collaboration among staff, volunteers, partners, and beneficiaries. - Community Ownership: We empower communities to lead literacy programs by training youth to champion sustainable interventions that align with local needs and priorities. - Partnerships: We collaborate with like-minded organizations and stakeholders to amplify the reach and impact of our programs, ensuring our values guide every initiative.
Objectives: - To improve foundational literacy skills amongchildren aged 2–12 years in underserved communities. - To build community-driven solutions by training and equipping youth as literacy champions and advocates. - To increase access to culturally relevant and affordable learning resources, including books, games, and digital tools. - To foster inclusion by targeting marginalized groups, including children with disabilities, refugees, and thosefrom low-income families.
